message.content:
{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: Node.js CI

on:
    push:
      branches: [ main ]
    pull_request:
      branches: [ main ]

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    strategy:
      matrix:
        node-version: [18.x, 20.x, 21.x]
        os: [ubuntu-latest, windows-latest, macos-latest]
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v3
    - uses: actions/setup-node@v3
      with:
        node-version: ${{ matrix.node-version }}
    - name: Cache npm dependencies
      uses: actions/cache@v4
      with:
        path: ~/.npm
        key: ${{ runner.os }}-node-${{ matrix.node-version }}-deps-${{ hashFiles('package-lock.json') }}
        restore-keys: |
          ${{ runner.os }}-node-${{ matrix.node-version }}-deps-
    - run: npm i
    - run: npm run lint
    - run: npm run build
    - run: npm test
    - name: Upload coverage to Codecov
      uses: codecov/codecov-action@v4
      with:
        token: ${{ secrets.CODECOV_TOKEN }}",
  "rationale": "The repository has a committed package-lock.json and installs dependencies with npm on every matrix job (3 node versions x 3 OS = 9 jobs), so repeated dependency fetching is a measurable cost and the lockfile provides a stable cache input. The P-LIT-GHA-CACHE pattern (dependency_cache) supports caching dependency downloads while keeping installation and all required tests, which preserves the existing lint/build/test/coverage coverage. A cache step keyed on runner OS, node version, and the package-lock.json hash is added before npm i; no steps are removed, no permissions are weakened, and no new secrets, publishing, deployment, or network targets are introduced.",
  "evidence_ids": ["P-LIT-GHA-CACHE"]
}
